planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed, once soil has warmed; Zowie Yellow Flame blooms fast from seed and holds its bicolor coloring best in full sun.

directions: Zowie Yellow Flame is an AAS-winning bicolor selection whose semi-double blooms open scarlet-red at the center and shade outward through orange to a golden-yellow petal tip, with the color pattern shifting as each flower ages so a single plant displays several tones at once. It branches freely on sturdy stems, making it useful both as a bedding standout and as a cut flower, and it keeps flowering from midsummer to frost with regular deadheading. Give it full sun and good air movement between plants to limit powdery mildew, the main disease pressure zinnias face in humid regions.

planting.note: Direct sow into lean, well-drained soil after last frost; Torch tolerates heat and dry spells better than large-flowered Zinnia elegans types.

directions: Torch is an heirloom Mexican zinnia bearing small, single to semi-double flowers in warm orange-red tones with a mahogany-red center ring, a color combination that has made it a long-standing garden classic since its early-20th-century introduction. Compared with large-flowered Zinnia elegans cultivars, Torch is more compact, more heat- and drought-tolerant, and noticeably more resistant to powdery mildew, so it performs well in humid or dry climates alike with minimal fuss. It self-sows readily and works well massed in borders, in wildflower-style plantings, or wherever a tough, long-blooming annual is needed with little supplemental water once established.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; Dreamland Scarlet flowers earlier and stays more compact than tall cut-flower zinnia types.

directions: Dreamland Scarlet was an early AAS-winning dwarf zinnia bred to bring the large, fully double flower form of tall cutting zinnias down onto a low, uniform bedding plant only about a foot tall. Its extra-large scarlet-red blooms open unusually quickly from seed relative to other zinnias, giving fast, reliable color in beds, edging, and containers. Because the flowers are large relative to the compact plant size, deadheading regularly keeps the display tidy and encourages continuous rebloom through the season.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in full sun; Pop Art's semi-dwarf habit needs no staking even with its large flower heads.

directions: Pop Art produces bold red single flowers heavily speckled and flecked with yellow, an unusual painterly pattern that sets it apart from the solid-colored or picotee-edged zinnias more commonly grown. The semi-dwarf, well-branched habit holds up the large flower heads without staking, and continuous bloom from midsummer to frost makes it a strong choice for both borders and cutting. It performs best with consistent deadheading and good airflow between plants to reduce powdery mildew in humid weather.

planting.note: Direct sow into lean soil after last frost; avoid rich or heavily fertilized beds, which push foliage growth at the expense of flowers.

directions: Psyche is a long-grown heirloom cosmos strain distinguished by semi-double and crested, ruffled-petal flowers in a mix of white, pink, and crimson, a fluffier texture than the flat single blooms of standard Cosmos bipinnatus. Plants keep the same tall, airy, finely cut foliage typical of the species and are just as easy from direct seed, thriving in poor, lean soil where richer conditions would produce excess foliage and fewer flowers. The ruffled flower form makes Psyche a favorite for cutting gardens and informal cottage borders where a bit of texture is wanted alongside classic single-flowered cosmos.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in full sun; Ladybird Scarlet's dwarf habit suits edging and containers where taller sulfur cosmos would overwhelm the space.

directions: Ladybird Scarlet is a dwarf, extra-compact selection of sulfur cosmos bred to bring the same heat- and drought-tolerant, brilliantly colored flowers of standard Cosmos sulphureus onto a low, tidy plant well under knee-height. Its vivid scarlet-orange single blooms open early and continue prolifically through summer heat that slows many other bedding annuals, and the short, well-branched habit needs no pinching or staking. It is well suited to the front of a border, edging, or containers, and its nectar-rich flowers draw butterflies and other pollinators throughout the season.
